UKRAINE ANIMAL RESCUE

By: Ntokozo Miya | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Amid the turmoil in Ukraine, a South African man risks his life to rescue wildlife from the danger zone – we explore how he executes his missions and why the threat of danger does not discourage him

Unique Selling Point:
Lionel has been recording his rescue efforts from Ukraine to neighbouring countries and South Africa. This footage will help us to visually represent his efforts and give viewers a sense of the conditions Lionel and his team are currently working under. We supplement these visuals with our own shot at the Simbonga Game Reserve, the sanctuary to which rescue animals from the Ukraine are brought.

Summary:
Lionel de Lange fell in love with and married Ukrainian national Anya. The couple has been living in Ukraine for 11 years. They spend a lot of time between South Africa and Ukraine.

The couple's love for animals led them to establish the Simbonga Game Reserve in Gqeberha in the Eastern Cape, a sanctuary for rescue animals. It is now also home to big cats rescued out of Ukraine.

Lionel's work is followed by many on social media but it is his recent rescue effort that attracted the attention of people across the globe. Lionel set about relocating Masha from Ukraine to neighbouring Romania just as Russia was making its way deeper into the Ukraine.

Masha entertained her Ukrainian countrymen for 19 years at a circus but when tensions intensified in the area, she was not a priority for rescue. In a daring endeavour, Lionel took it upon himself to ensure that Masha is removed from the threat of Russian firepower and starvation and taken to her forever home in Romania.

Lionel paints an interesting picture of his second home in the Ukraine and puts into context why he is rescuing so many big cats from that country.

In the Ukraine, big cats are a status symbol. Lionel says it's an 'I've arrived, I've made it' statement among the country's rich.

Unfortunately, when tensions intensified, big cat owners were so overwhelmed by challenges trying to keep themselves and their families safe that their cats were neglected. The pets were a logistical complication that could not be overcome. Sadly, the owners were forced to leave their beloved pets behind.

Lionel is giving those animals a second shot at a safe, carefree life in South Africa where they are cared for by skilled and experienced staff at the Gqeberha reserve.

Further information:
Lionel is in South Africa for the next 10 days. Thereafter, he will return to Ukraine to begin the administrative process for the transfer and transport of lions Simba and Mir to South Africa.

Interestingly, Lionel came across Mir during the rescue of Masha the bear and did not have the heart to abandon the lion.

Over and above Lionel's footage, we capture the South African preparations for the arrival of the next batch of Ukrainian animals. We also get updates on how the animals who are already at the reserve are adjusting to their new surroundings.

Another unique aspect that Lionel brings to the piece is that he will take viewers into Ukraine and share the mood of the country that has been his home for many years. He is able to give insight into the situation on the ground for locals and foreign nationals as they navigate their way out of the country, leaving behind their homes and uncertain if and when they will return.

In South Africa, we also speak to other members of the team that receives the rescued animals in Gqeberha.

Extra Budget Items:
Ruan is available to travel to PE. Like Peter, he is ideal for shoots with a lot of movement and is also well-equipped to get us the cinematic shots that will make the piece special. He shot the elephant gin story.

I have pencil-booked Mac and will be getting travel and accomodation quotes by latest tomorrow.

Script:


LIONEL – APPROVED FINAL FOR MIX

AUDIO
INTRO – Lionel De Lange is one of those rare individuals willing to risk everything for love.

After finding a match on an online dating site, he packed up his life in South Africa and moved to Ukraine more than a decade ago. But while he loved the country and decided to stay, the relationship fizzled.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
It didn't work out with the two of us, you know, we were just too different.
VO - But the stars aligned three years later, when he met Anya Masyach - who would later become his wife.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
Anya and I opened a couple of little seasonal coffee shops, and in fact, that's where we ended up with our four homeless dogs and cats.
VO - Lionel and Anya shared a simple, happy life with their beloved pets in the southern town of Kherson… little knowing it would one day be thrown into turmoil.
UPSOUND – NEWS REPORTS - WAR VISUALS – DRAMA!!!

“And tonight new revelations about Russia's potential new war plan to control all of southern Ukraine.”
“Ukraine says elite Russian units are now moving in.”
VO - After years of simmering tensions, Russian forces invaded Ukraine in late February this year.
UPSOUNDS - EXPLOSIONS AND OTHER NAT AUDIO FROM B-ROLL

“Russian troops are attacking from the north, south and east.”

“Military bases, airports and aircrafts have been targeted and bombed.”
VO - Local forces fought back, and the conflict spread along multiple fronts across the country.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
CLAIRE - It must have been so surreal then for you being there at the time of war breaking out...
LIONEL - I thought, well, I better get to the shop quickly and buy some extra milk and maybe two loaves of bread. It didn't really sink in. The banks restricted how much money you could withdraw each day. We were only allowed to put 20 litres of fuel in the car at a time and the supermarkets were completely overrun.
VO – Lionel made it out of Ukraine. He returned to South Africa where his wife had been waiting, leaving behind friends and family.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
LIONEL - I made sure that Anya's grandparents were okay and they would never leave. I mean, they are too old, you know. [sigh] And I had to leave them. [cries]
CLAIRE – I mean, you've got people there. You've got friends, family. Have they decided to stay like Anya's grandparents?

LIONEL – No, I think it's 50/50. A lot of friends have stayed and many of them have run as well. But some of them just stayed in place because they've got nowhere to go.
VO - Many refugees fled with their pets, but Ukrainians are also fascinated by exotic animals. What of them?
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST

There's a big problem with private ownership of lions in Ukraine. The guy will have a restaurant and he will have a lion or a bear in a cage outside to attract people.
VO – Ukrainians can buy a range of wildlife online, including big cat cubs.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST

And then the cat gets too big and that's where the problem comes in. They'll just dump them anywhere or shoot them or sell them to someone else, give them as a gift. There are tigers and lions and bears living in people's houses in Ukraine.
BREATHER – UPSOUND – LIONEL AND ANYA

From the Warriors of Wildlife team in Ukraine...
VO – Back in 2014, he and Anya founded the Warriors of Wildlife with a mission to re- home unwanted exotics. But they inevitably battled to find new homes for the animals in Ukraine, and eventually established the Simbonga Game Reserve and Sanctuary here in the Eastern Cape. It became a home in the sun for some of Ukraine’s big cats.

So, when war descended on his adoptive country, Lionel sprung into action.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
I feel for the animals. I don't want to say I don't feel for people, but there's so many organizations helping people and so few helping animals.
LINK - There are many, many repercussions to a conflict - if people are leaving, and if food is scarce and if we are all thinking about survival, the animals suffer. I don't think that even crossed my mind before coming here and speaking to Lionel.
VO - Among the animals suffering as a result of the conflict was a very special bear; one Lionel had already rescued once and was determined to do so again
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
We're on the road from Bucharest to Halmeu border post. We're on our way to get Masha. This mission is on.
VO – ...and a daring mission it was – Lionel and his team snuck back into Ukraine via Romania to smuggle Masha the bear out of the war zone and into safety. In 2018, after 19 years of intolerable abuse at a circus, Lionel had taken Masha to a town called Sambir in the west of the country. He could not have known he would risk his life just 4 years later to ensure her safety.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
It's just not 100% safe and nobody really knows what's going on.
VO - The threat of Russian firepower is real – as of the 26th of April, close to three thousand civilian deaths were reported and over three thousand people have been injured.

Once in Ukraine, they manoeuvred around possible military targets to get to Masha.
INTENSE, DRAMATIC MUSIC
VO – Thankfully, they reached Masha safely… relieved to find her unharmed
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
Mash, say 'hello' to everyone. Are you okay, girl?
VO – After preparing Masha for the risky trip ahead, they drove through the night, stopping only occasionally to allow her some fresh air.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
We're in Mochakuva about an hour and 20 minutes from the Romanian border. This is Masha's last morning in Ukraine.
VO – Miraculously, they made it to the border and out of Ukraine without incident.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
We were there for a couple of hours and the doors of the van were open, and it brought smiles to their faces, crying children and unhappy people, and then they saw Masha and they sort of understood, well, she's also a refugee, just like they are.
VO – After another grueling trip from the border to the town of Zarnesti in Romania, Masha finally arrived at her forever home, the Liberty Bear Sanctuary.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
At least I can go home back to South Africa and know that she is safe.
VO – While in South Africa, Lionel spends his days at Simbonga, caring for the big cats with anotherhusband and wife team, Keegan and Lauren Smith.
LAUREN VAD-SMITH – SIMBONGA SANCTUARY MANAGER

All of the enclosures you guys are seeing, that was us on the ground while he was busy with the rescues in Ukraine. We have a lot of friends and family that come out and they help us do everything from digging holes in the ground, putting these fences up, putting up their night shelters, the gates
VO - The hard labour aside, getting the lions from Ukraine is pricey.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
The last five lions that we brought out now was $38,000 just for the flights. But then it's the feeding prior to that. A cat will eat between five and seven kilos of meat today. You're around $1000 a month.
VO – The sanctuary receives donations of meat from farmers in the area. Keegan oversees meal time.
KEEGAN SMITH – SIMBONGA SANCTUARY MANAGER
KEEGAN - So we've got Panthera supplement, which is just an all round multivitamin basically, and then we've got some calcium. We just have to make a couple of deep slits so that the powder can be in the meat to absorb properly.
CLAIRE - What are some of the dietary issues that some of these big cats have come in with?

KEEGAN - Some of the cats were fed a predominantly turkey diet and that's not normal for the cats. Typically they need that red meat.
VO – The sound of the van is a meal-time siren for the newcomers
MEAL-TIME VIZ AND UPSOUNDS
[Keegan throws a piece of meat into lion's shelter, Lauren locks the gate behind him.]
CLAIRE – [opens second gate] Lunch is served.
[Lion walks into shelter, shot of 3 lions eating, close-up on one]
LINK - Sometimes even after all the effort and care that's put into rescuing these animals, unfortunately, survival is not always guaranteed.
VO – That’s true of the cats and - tragically - it was true of Masha the bear. Just three weeks after moving into her new home, Lionel got the bad news.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
She had a stroke and she passed away. [pause] We can only assume that it was stress because she was healthy, she was fed well
VO – While heartbroken, Lionel is already preparing to head back to Ukraine to rescue two more big cats.
LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST
CLAIRE - Describe the feeling of seeing the cats arrive from Ukraine after months of work, forms, stress, phone calls, emails.

LIONEL - That makes all the stress, all the issues, all the hate, all the fighting - it makes everything just disappear when they step out for the first time. The feeling is indescribable. Those experiences make everything worthwhile.

TEASER / PROMO 1
LIONEL: We're in Mochakuva about an hour and 20 minutes from the Romanian border.
VO: One South African man and his team.... a bear in distress... and the journey to smuggle this mammal out of a war!
LIONEL: This mission is on.
TEASER / PROMO 2
VO: How do you smuggle a full-grown bear out of a war-torn country?
LIONEL: It's just not 100% safe and nobody really knows what's going on. and that's where the problem comes in.
VO: One South African nature conservationist dared to find out...
LIONEL: I feel for the animals. There's so many organizations helping people and so few helping animals.
TEASER / PROMO 3
VO: As millions of Ukrainians flee their country... one South African man is determined to get back into the war-zone....
LIONEL: We're on the road from Bucharest to Halmeu border post.
VO: His mission? To save refugees .... of a different kind.

VO - The threat of Russian firepower is real – as of the 26th of April, close to three thousand civilian deaths were reported and over three thousand people have been injured. Once in Ukraine, they manoeuvred around possible military targets to get to Masha. INTENSE, DRAMATIC MUSIC VO – Thankfully, they reached Masha safely… relieved to find her unharmed LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST Mash, say 'hello' to everyone. Are you okay, girl? VO – After preparing Masha for the risky trip ahead, they drove through the night, stopping only occasionally to allow her some fresh air. LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST We're in Mochakuva about an hour and 20 minutes from the Romanian border. This is Masha's last morning in Ukraine. VO – Miraculously, they made it to the border and out of Ukraine without incident. LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST We were there for a couple of hours and the doors of the van were open, and it brought smiles to their faces, crying children and unhappy people, and then they saw Masha and they sort of understood, well, she's also a refugee, just like they are. VO – After another grueling trip from the border to the town of Zarnesti in Romania, Masha finally arrived at her forever home, the Liberty Bear Sanctuary. LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST At least I can go home back to South Africa and know that she is safe. VO – While in South Africa, Lionel spends his days at Simbonga, caring for the big cats with anotherhusband and wife team, Keegan and Lauren Smith. LAUREN VAD-SMITH – SIMBONGA SANCTUARY MANAGER All of the enclosures you guys are seeing, that was us on the ground while he was busy with the rescues in Ukraine. We have a lot of friends and family that come out and they help us do everything from digging holes in the ground, putting these fences up, putting up their night shelters, the gates VO - The hard labour aside, getting the lions from Ukraine is pricey. LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST The last five lions that we brought out now was $38,000 just for the flights. But then it's the feeding prior to that. A cat will eat between five and seven kilos of meat today. You're around $1000 a month. VO – The sanctuary receives donations of meat from farmers in the area. Keegan oversees meal time. KEEGAN SMITH – SIMBONGA SANCTUARY MANAGER KEEGAN - So we've got Panthera supplement, which is just an all round multivitamin basically, and then we've got some calcium. We just have to make a couple of deep slits so that the powder can be in the meat to absorb properly. CLAIRE - What are some of the dietary issues that some of these big cats have come in with? KEEGAN - Some of the cats were fed a predominantly turkey diet and that's not normal for the cats. Typically they need that red meat. VO – The sound of the van is a meal-time siren for the newcomers MEAL-TIME VIZ AND UPSOUNDS [Keegan throws a piece of meat into lion's shelter, Lauren locks the gate behind him.] CLAIRE – [opens second gate] Lunch is served. [Lion walks into shelter, shot of 3 lions eating, close-up on one] LINK - Sometimes even after all the effort and care that's put into rescuing these animals, unfortunately, survival is not always guaranteed. VO – That’s true of the cats and - tragically - it was true of Masha the bear. Just three weeks after moving into her new home, Lionel got the bad news. LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST She had a stroke and she passed away. [pause] We can only assume that it was stress because she was healthy, she was fed well VO – While heartbroken, Lionel is already preparing to head back to Ukraine to rescue two more big cats. LIONEL DE LANGE – WILDLIFE RESCUE ACTIVIST CLAIRE - Describe the feeling of seeing the cats arrive from Ukraine after months of work, forms, stress, phone calls, emails. LIONEL - That makes all the stress, all the issues, all the hate, all the fighting - it makes everything just disappear when they step out for the first time. The feeling is indescribable. Those experiences make everything worthwhile. TEASER / PROMO 1 LIONEL: We're in Mochakuva about an hour and 20 minutes from the Romanian border. VO: One South African man and his team.... a bear in distress... and the journey to smuggle this mammal out of a war! LIONEL: This mission is on. TEASER / PROMO 2 VO: How do you smuggle a full-grown bear out of a war-torn country? LIONEL: It's just not 100% safe and nobody really knows what's going on. and that's where the problem comes in. VO: One South African nature conservationist dared to find out... LIONEL: I feel for the animals. There's so many organizations helping people and so few helping animals. TEASER / PROMO 3 VO: As millions of Ukrainians flee their country... one South African man is determined to get back into the war-zone.... LIONEL: We're on the road from Bucharest to Halmeu border post. VO: His mission? To save refugees .... of a different kind.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Amid the turmoil in Ukraine, a South African man risks his life to rescue wildlife from the danger zone – we explore how he executes his missions and why the threat of danger does not discourage him
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Lionel has been recording his rescue efforts from Ukraine to neighbouring countries and South Africa. This footage will help us to visually represent his efforts and give viewers a sense of the conditions Lionel and his team are currently working under. We supplement these visuals with our own shot at the Simbonga Game Reserve, the sanctuary to which rescue animals from the Ukraine are brought.
metadata.Summary: Lionel de Lange fell in love with and married Ukrainian national Anya. The couple has been living in Ukraine for 11 years. They spend a lot of time between South Africa and Ukraine. The couple's love for animals led them to establish the Simbonga Game Reserve in Gqeberha in the Eastern Cape, a sanctuary for rescue animals. It is now also home to big cats rescued out of Ukraine. Lionel's work is followed by many on social media but it is his recent rescue effort that attracted the attention of people across the globe. Lionel set about relocating Masha from Ukraine to neighbouring Romania just as Russia was making its way deeper into the Ukraine. Masha entertained her Ukrainian countrymen for 19 years at a circus but when tensions intensified in the area, she was not a priority for rescue. In a daring endeavour, Lionel took it upon himself to ensure that Masha is removed from the threat of Russian firepower and starvation and taken to her forever home in Romania. Lionel paints an interesting picture of his second home in the Ukraine and puts into context why he is rescuing so many big cats from that country. In the Ukraine, big cats are a status symbol. Lionel says it's an 'I've arrived, I've made it' statement among the country's rich. Unfortunately, when tensions intensified, big cat owners were so overwhelmed by challenges trying to keep themselves and their families safe that their cats were neglected. The pets were a logistical complication that could not be overcome. Sadly, the owners were forced to leave their beloved pets behind. Lionel is giving those animals a second shot at a safe, carefree life in South Africa where they are cared for by skilled and experienced staff at the Gqeberha reserve.
metadata.Further information: Lionel is in South Africa for the next 10 days. Thereafter, he will return to Ukraine to begin the administrative process for the transfer and transport of lions Simba and Mir to South Africa. Interestingly, Lionel came across Mir during the rescue of Masha the bear and did not have the heart to abandon the lion. Over and above Lionel's footage, we capture the South African preparations for the arrival of the next batch of Ukrainian animals. We also get updates on how the animals who are already at the reserve are adjusting to their new surroundings. Another unique aspect that Lionel brings to the piece is that he will take viewers into Ukraine and share the mood of the country that has been his home for many years. He is able to give insight into the situation on the ground for locals and foreign nationals as they navigate their way out of the country, leaving behind their homes and uncertain if and when they will return. In South Africa, we also speak to other members of the team that receives the rescued animals in Gqeberha.
